$comment: The canonical spelling of an OPC UA node id, and how a namespace-URI form resolves against a server's NamespaceArray. Both runtimes must agree case for case, because both read the *same* policy file: a form one canonicalises and the other does not is an allowlist that authorises different writes depending on which server the operator happened to start. tests/unit/test_node_ids.py and the "node id forms" suite in packages/server-node/test/unit.test.mjs each read this file and may skip no case, so adding one here forces both runtimes to handle it.

canonical.name: zero namespace restored
canonical.note: python-opcua omits ns=0 from to_string() while node-opcua writes it, so the same node arrives spelled two ways. Compared raw, an allowlist entry in one form silently never matches the other.

canonical.name: surrounding whitespace trimmed
canonical.note: A CSV allowlist written `ns=2;i=5, ns=2;i=6` has a leading space on every entry after the first.

canonical.name: namespace-URI form left for resolution
canonical.note: Canonicalisation does not resolve; that needs the server's NamespaceArray and happens separately.

canonical.name: expanded node id with a server index untouched
canonical.note: No implicit zero namespace to restore, and rewriting what is already explicit risks changing its meaning.

resolved.name: index form in a non-zero namespace
namespace URI resolved to its index
resolved.note: The stable name resolved to this session's index. This is the whole point of the form: a firmware update that reorders the NamespaceArray moves the index, and the allowlist follows it.

resolved.name: namespace URI for the third namespace
resolved.note: An `s=` identifier may itself contain no ';' here, but the split is on the first ';' only so that identifiers which do are not truncated.

resolved.name: unknown namespace URI resolves to nothing
resolved.note: A real answer, not a failure to compute one: the entry names a namespace this server does not publish, so nothing can match it and the policy must deny rather than fall back to something that looks close.

resolved.name: malformed namespace-URI form with no identifier
resolved.note: Not the nsu= form at all without a ';', so it is left alone and will simply match nothing.
